items.summary: Cisco Nexus 3000 and 9000 Series switches: an unauthenticated, remote attacker can execute arbitrary code via crafted MPLS OAM packets, disclosed in Cisco's October 7 NX-OS security bundle. Switches are management-plane-adjacent, so patching should take priority in enterprise networks.

Cisco NX-OS Software NX-API remote code execution: unauthenticated attackers can run arbitrary commands with elevated privileges through the NX-API interface on Nexus switches. Part of the same October 7 Cisco bundle; exposed management APIs make this a strong wormable target.

IBM Security Verify Access 10.0 through 10.0.9.2 and IBM Verify Identity Access 11.0 through 11.0.3: an insecure deserialization flaw lets a remote unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code, disclosed October 8. Identity infrastructure is a crown jewel, so treat this as an emergency patch.

dot-access (npm package, versions 0.0.3 through 1.0.0): code injection via crafted paths supplied to the get() function lets a remote attacker execute arbitrary JavaScript, disclosed October 8. Any Node.js app taking filesystem paths from user input should audit and update the dependency.

Atlassian Data Center flaw: an unauthenticated arbitrary file access vulnerability across eight products (Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible, Fisheye), disclosed October 5. Honeypots recorded exploitation attempts within two hours of technical details going public, so self-managed instances should patch immediately.
